predecessors.note: 'established around 1600 as an offshoot of the royal dynasty of the Kingdom of Allada'.

land.text: the kingdom, made 'a French protectorate in 1894'; the kingdom under Agoli-agbo lasted as a protectorate to 1904 when it became French Dahomey

successors.note: Infobox: French Protectorate (1894-1904). The page's king table carries Agoli-agbo to 1900; the protectorate tint belongs to the French dossier.

capitals.name: Abomey
capitals.note: Infobox capital Abomey; the French entered the capital on 17 November 1892 (Second Franco-Dahomean War page).

correction.text: Aja settlers from Allada settle on the Abomey Plateau about 1600

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox: 'Aja settlers from Allada settle on Abomey Plateau: c. 1600'; the page gives no extent, so a 20 km circle round Abomey stands for the first settlement.

correction.text: the Abomey Plateau after Dakodonou's conquest; infobox area 10,000 km2 in 1700

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Dakodonu begins conquest on Abomey Plateau: c. 1620'. The infobox gives 10,000 km2 in 1700; a 56 km circle round Abomey is about 9,850 km2, chosen to match it (so this is a fit to the infobox, not a check). The Dahomey page names no towns for the plateau.

correction.text: the plateau plus Allada and Godomey, conquered in March-April 1724

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On March 30, 1724, Agaja's army entered Allada'; 'In April 1724, Agaja conquered the town of Godomey'. Atlantique department without a 40 km circle round Ouidah stands for the Allada kingdom (about 2,500 km2 in all); the page gives no frontier for Allada.

correction.text: the plateau plus the whole of Atlantique, with the coast at Whydah (Ouidah) after 26 February 1727

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'On February 26, 1727, Agaja attacked Whydah and burned the palace.' The Oyo boundary after 1730 was 'the Ouemé River' (Agaja page); the northern conquests (the Mahi war from 1731) and the tributary Porto-Novo are not placed because no page gives their land. Infobox gives no area after 1700.

correction.text: the kingdom after the cession of Cotonou, 3 October 1890

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Béhanzin was also forced to cede Cotonou, but did receive 20,000 francs a year for giving up his customs rights.' A 12 km circle round Cotonou goes to the French. The French entered Abomey on 17 November 1892 and Behanzin fought on in the north until 15 January 1894; the page gives no territorial division between 1892 and 1894, so the shape holds to the surrender.

ledger.note: c. 1600: the Kingdom of Dahomey is founded on the Abomey Plateau. 'The Kingdom of Dahomey was established around 1600 as an offshoot of the royal dynasty of the Kingdom of Allada'; infobox 'Aja settlers from Allada settle on Abomey Plateau: c. 1600'. The page treats Houegbadja (c. 1645-1685) as the foundational king.
c. 1620: Dakodonou begins the conquest of the Abomey Plateau. Infobox: 'Dakodonu begins conquest on Abomey Plateau: c. 1620'. The 10,000 km2 infobox area of 1700 is the plateau at its first extent.

region.text: the Kingdom of Allada and Godomey; Atlantique department without Whydah

ledger.note: 1724 (30 March): Agaja takes Allada, the mother kingdom. 'On March 30, 1724, Agaja's army entered Allada'; 'In April 1724, Agaja conquered the town of Godomey'. The Dahomey page: 'In 1724, Agaja conquered Allada'.

region.text: the Abomey Plateau, the Dahomey heartland

ledger.note: 1726 (14 April): Oyo sends its army against Dahomey and sacks Abomey. 'on April 14, 1726, the Oyo Empire sent its army against Dahomey'; again on 22 March 1728, 1729 and 1730, the most damaging.

region.text: the Kingdom of Whydah round Ouidah and its coast

ledger.note: 1727 (26 February): Agaja takes Whydah, the slave-trading port. 'On February 26, 1727, Agaja attacked Whydah and burned the palace'; Dahomey page: 'in 1727 he conquered Whydah'.

region.text: Whydah, disputed by Huffon and the exiled royal family

ledger.note: 1730 (about): the Whydah exiles try to retake the coast. 'After the 1730 Oyo attack, Huffon and the exiled royal family tried to retake Whydah with British and French support'; the page gives no year for the attempt, so 1730 is bridging.

region.text: the kingdom of Dahomey, tributary of Oyo

ledger.note: 1730: Dahomey becomes a tributary of Oyo. Infobox 'vassal state of the Oyo Empire (1730-1823)'; the text says 'Dahomey became a tributary of the Oyo from 1732 until 1823' and elsewhere 'since 1748' (the oyo-empire dossier uses 1748). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of oyo-empire's vassal events.
1734: the last Whydah faction is beaten. 'The other Whydah faction was defeated by Agaja in 1734,' with French assistance; Huffon had died in July 1733 and the exiles had split.

1740: the Oyo war ends with Agaja's death. Agaja 'died in Allada a few months after returning following the war with Oyo in 1740'; the Dahomey page has 'near constant warfare with ... the Oyo Empire, from 1728 until 1740'. Dahomey pays tribute afterwards (dates conflict: 1730, 1732 or 1748 to 1823 or 1827).

region.text: the kingdom of Dahomey, tributary of Oyo

ledger.note: 1823: Dahomey stops paying tribute to Oyo ('a tributary of the Oyo from 1732 until 1823'; infobox 1730-1823). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of oyo-empire 1823 vassal_end.

region.text: the kingdom of Porto-Novo, tributary of Dahomey

ledger.note: 1861: Porto-Novo is named as one of Dahomey's tributaries. 'In 1861, the kingdom of Porto-Novo, one of Dahomey's tributaries, was bombarded by the Royal Navy.' The page does not say when the tribute began.
1863: Porto-Novo becomes a French protectorate. 'Porto-Novo became a French protectorate in 1863.' Dahomey recognised it on 3 October 1890.

1890 (4 March): Dahomey storms the French stockade at Cotonou. 'On 4 March, a Dahomey army of several thousand charged the log stockade around Cotonou'; the French had arrested Fon officials there on 21 February.
1890 (3 October): Dahomey cedes Cotonou to France. 'Béhanzin was also forced to cede Cotonou, but did receive 20,000 francs a year for giving up his customs rights.'
1890 (3 October): the first war ends in a treaty. 'On 3 October 1890, Dahomey signed a treaty recognising the kingdom of Porto-Novo as a French protectorate.'

region.text: the kingdom of Dahomey from the coast to Abomey

ledger.note: 1892 (4 July): the second war begins. 'on 4 July, the first shots of the war were fired from French gunboats'; the French entered Abomey on 17 November 1892.
1894 (15 January): Behanzin surrenders. 'King Béhanzin surrendered to the French on 15 January 1894 and was exiled to Martinique.'

1894: Dahomey is reduced and made a French protectorate. 'The kingdom was reduced and made a French protectorate in 1894'; 'the French chose Béhanzin's brother, Goutchili, as the new king' (Second war page). In 1904 the area became French Dahomey.

region.text: the kingdom, to French protectorate and then French Dahomey

ledger.note: 1894 (January): the independent Kingdom of Dahomey ends; a French protectorate with Agoli-agbo as king runs to 1904. 'The kingdom was defeated in 1894.'

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Allada
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Agaja's army entered Allada on 30 March 1724 and took Godomey in April.

wars.name: Dahomean conquest of Whydah
wars.outcome: Dahomey won: Whydah attacked 26 February 1727, palace burned; the exiles under Huffon failed to retake it (Huffon d. July 1733) and the last faction was beaten in 1734.

wars.name: Oyo invasions of Dahomey
wars.outcome: Oyo sacked Abomey in 1726 and invaded again in 1728, 1729 and 1730; Dahomey became a tributary state with the boundary at the Ouémé River, and Agaja sent his son Tegbessou to Oyo as a guarantee; war resumed in 1739 and ended 1740.
wars.note: Tribute dates conflict across the Dahomey page: 'since 1748' (Ghezo section), 'from 1732 until 1823' (Oyo section) and 1730-1823 (infobox); the tribute ended in 1823 (infobox) or 1827, 'at Paonignan'. The Agaja page says the status 'would remain until 1832'.

wars.name: Dahomean war against the Mahi
wars.outcome: A war against the Mahi people, north of Abomey, began in 1731; the Agaja page gives no outcome or land.
wars.note: Godomey was burned in 1732 and Badagry attacked in 1737 (against the Dutch); no land change is recorded.

wars.name: First Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: Cotonou ceded and Porto-Novo recognised as a French protectorate in the treaty of 3 October 1890.

wars.name: Second Franco-Dahomean War
wars.outcome: French victory: Abomey entered 17 November 1892; Béhanzin surrendered 15 January 1894 and was exiled to Martinique; Dahomey became a French protectorate.

certainty.note: No frontier line is given by the pages; the Ouémé River boundary with Oyo after 1730 (Agaja page) and the Cotonou cession of 3 October 1890 are the only treaty-fixed edges, and neither is drawn sharp.

notes: Dahomey has no Cliopatria row; the Oyo dossier (af-04-a) draws Dahomey inside the Oyo shapes of 1752-1835. Five pages opened (the budget). Disagreements: founding 'approximately 1600' and Houegbadja as 'foundational king' (c. 1645-1685 in the text, 1645-1680 in the table); Agaja 1708-1740 (table) vs 1718-1740 (Agaja page); the Oyo tribute 1730, 1732 or 1748 to 1823, 1827 or 1832; the Oyo dossier has contest 1728-1748 against this dossier's 1726-1740 (the Agaja page dates the first Oyo army 14 April 1726). The infobox 10,000 km2 (1700) fixes only the plateau's size; the pages give no later area, no Mahi or Weme conquests and no Abeokuta war dates (the Dahomey page names an 1864 operation against Abeokuta without a result). Not placed: Mahi, Weme/Porto-Novo coast, Badagry. The Atlantique department stands for Allada and Whydah (Whydah itself 40 km round Ouidah). The 1894-1904 protectorate under Agoli-agbo is left to the French dossier; the Second war page does not give his installation. Counterpart slugs without a dossier in this batch: kingdom-of-allada, kingdom-of-whydah, kingdom-of-porto-novo (these may be written by this group later; check).
